crossRefs.note: But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised by the people.
All those who see me mock me. They insult me with their lips. They shake their heads, saying,
I can count all of my bones. They look and stare at me.
Because of all my adversaries I have become utterly contemptible to my neighbors, a horror to my acquaintances. Those…
But in my adversity, they rejoiced, and gathered themselves together. The attackers gathered themselves together…
Because for your sake, I have borne reproach. Shame has covered my face.
Reproach has broken my heart, and I am full of heaviness. I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; for…
for they have opened the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of deceit against me. They have spoken to me with a lying…
I have also become a reproach to them. When they see me, they shake their head.
“Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look, and see if there is any sorrow like my sorrow, which is brought on…
All that pass by clap their hands at you. They hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying, “Is this…
Those who passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads, and saying, “Ha! You who destroy the temple, and build it in…
save yourself, and come down from the cross!”
The people stood watching. The rulers with them also scoffed at him, saying, “He saved others. Let him save himself, if…
who didn’t sin, “neither was deceit found in his mouth.”
